title: Clean DCP Polynomial-Pool CNOT Collimation Sieve: Exact 1/2 Sign-Branching Law, Bucket-Pairing Capacity, and Superpolynomial Depth Barrier

theorems.statement: For any secret S in Z_q^n, labels a_1, a_2 in Z_q^n, and visibilities v_1, v_2 in [0, 1], applying CNOT_{1->2} to rho_{a_1}(S, v_1) otimes rho_{a_2}(S, v_2) and measuring qubit 2 in the Z basis yields z in {0, 1} with Pr[z=0] = Pr[z=1] = 1/2 and conditional state rho_{(a_1 + (-1)^z a_2) mod q}(S, v_1 v_2). When a_1 == a_2 mod 2^b with 2 a_2 != 0 mod 2^b, only z=1 cancels the low b bits, so 2 consumed parents yield at most 1/2 expected collimated child.

In a pool of M_pool independent qubits distributed uniformly across B = 2^b buckets with occupancies (c_0, ..., c_{B-1}), the maximum number of disjoint matched pairs is N_pairs(c) = sum_{u=0}^{B-1} floor(c_u / 2) <= floor(M_pool / 2), with E[N_pairs] <= min(M_pool / 2, C(M_pool, 2) / B) and expected surviving subtraction children E[M_child] = E[N_pairs] / 2 <= min(M_pool / 4, M_pool(M_pool - 1)/(4 B)).

Cancelling nt - 1 label bits using polynomial pools of size M_pool (which cancel at most b = floor(log_2 C(M_pool, 2)) bits per level) requires tree depth L_min = ceil((nt - 1)/b) = Omega(nt / log(nt)) and expected initial preparations >= 4^{L_min} = 2^{2 ceil((nt - 1)/b)} = 2^{Omega(nt / log(nt))}, strictly worse than Kuperberg's subexponential collimation sieve 2^{Theta(sqrt(nt))}.
